structured_assessments.method: Complete TOML parse; unique package identities, registry source/checksum counts; not dependency-source audit
Complete XML parse and embedded JPEG base64/signature validation; not visual inspection

findings: Three core modules fully read. exact_hash hashes extracted canonical text; byte_hash hashes supplied bytes only as a separate API/fallback. Text-hash equality must not be relabeled original-file equality. There is no source stability or file reading in this module.

Near matching normalizes lower case and whitespace, builds character five-grams and 128 MinHash values. Exact Jaccard here is exact over deduplicated 64-bit shingle hashes, not raw text or collision-free original shingles. DefaultHasher stability across calls is insufficient as a persisted cross-Rust-version format guarantee.

Containment uses the smaller-side relationship with a separate 0.96 threshold and 0.40 Jaccard floor by default, to limit shared-template/fragment links. Family caller enforcement remains unread. MinHash candidate threshold 0.80 is heuristic and not itself complete retrieval proof.

overlap_at_least bounds possible remaining intersection using sorted unique inputs; public slice functions rely on their documented sorted/deduplicated precondition without checking it. Empty/empty Jaccard=1 while containment empty denominator=0. Six authored near tests cover a Korean proposal, one edit, appendix, empty and unrelated texts plus one set example; no suite executed.

family.rs lines 1..580 read. Text-exact components trust supplied digest strings for comparable documents; noncomparable docs trust optional byte-hash strings. No original-byte confirmation occurs here. Public from_precomputed also trusts supplied digest/signature/shingle ordering and consistency.

Candidate retrieval uses 16x8 MinHash LSH and a bottom-64 index that drops postings present in more than 64 documents. Verification only removes false candidates; it cannot restore omitted true pairs. Source explicitly estimates probabilistic LSH recall, so all-pairs near/containment completeness is unproven.

Union-find produces transitive connected components, not pairwise-similar cliques. Candidates already in the same component are skipped at each chunk boundary, so the documented every verified pair evidence is not every qualifying pair; evidence subset and strongest-member relation can depend on input ordering/chunk boundaries. Parallel scheduling is stabilized for fixed input order.

One merge intersect calculates both containment directions and Jaccard with early upper-bound rejection, a useful shared-computation idea. Public config fields have no finite/range validation in inspected code. FamilyLabel derives strongest per-member relations rather than all edge relation kinds; exact-star edges and synthetic exact scores describe text/hash identity, not all original-file byte equality. Tests below line 580 remain unread; no suite run.

Completed family.rs. Tests use authored Korean proposal/noise/template corpora: selected template siblings stay separate, draft/appendix containment joins, member evidence endpoints and mixed labels are checked, and empty-text byte fallback uses literal pdf/pdf-a/pdf-b strings rather than actual PDFs.

Determinism test repeats the same input order eight times and compares IDs/member paths/edge counts/labels, not every edge endpoint/score, input permutations or explicit Rayon thread pools. The parallel minimum-work branch is not asserted reached. Transitive test verifies one component size only and does not establish that endpoints are below threshold.

Candidate tests search a finite authored edit range for a MinHash underestimate, inject identical signatures to model overestimate, and assert one contains case LSH might miss, without proving LSH actually omitted it. No >64-document posting-cap recall or exhaustive brute-force candidate oracle is present. Hash-sketch length bound is not a total memory bound.

Useful mechanisms to consider independently: retain per-pair relation evidence, distinguish mixed families, compute overlap metrics in one merge pass and apply a separate Jaccard floor to containment. Full retrieval completeness, byte identity and platform/format qualification remain separate. No upstream tests executed.

Rank module and nine authored tests fully read. Effective time prefers each file internal modified timestamp over filesystem mtime; unique latest receives score1 and fixed confidence0.9, ties/missing receive confidence0.5. These confidence values are heuristic constants, not calibrated probabilities. A single known timestamp among missing timestamps can be called unique latest. It is a candidate ordering, not proof of newest semantic version or safe keeper choice.

Extension-only dispatch recognizes eight document/text formats; extract_ready returns true for supported enum variants and is not a corpus validation gate. Plain text reads the entire file into memory, rejects invalid UTF8 and normalizes CRLF/CR; resulting text-exact equality intentionally differs from original byte equality. No size cap, cancellation or before/after source stamp is visible in this path.

Plain-text test writes a fixed temp filename dupey-extract-test.txt rather than a unique test directory, with possible concurrent collision; it checks newline normalization only. Format-specific extractors remain unread. No upstream tests executed.

DOCX extractor fully read. Reads only word/document.xml paragraph text and optional core metadata; headers, footers and other package parts do not participate. Text identity therefore cannot establish complete document identity. It matches local XML tag names without namespace validation, omits explicit tab/break handling and only consumes Text events while inside a t element.

DOCX XML parse errors break the parser and return accumulated text as success; text decode failures are silently skipped. Optional core entry errors are discarded with ok(). Corrupt or partially parsed files can therefore contribute apparently successful partial canonical text. No decompressed-size cap, cancellation or source-stability receipt is present in this extractor.

Three DOCX test definitions inspect generated Korean paragraphs, metadata and equality after changed core metadata. They do not cover malformed XML, decompression limits, namespace confusion, tabs, line breaks or header/footer differences. The volatile-parts test comment mentions changed app.xml noise, but fixture builder writes identical app.xml bytes in both archives. Upstream tests were not executed.

PPTX extractor fully read. Discovers slide XML by archive filename prefix/suffix and sorts numeric filename suffixes, rather than consulting presentation.xml slide IDs and relationships. Reordered slide sequences, unreferenced slide parts and nonnumeric matching names are therefore not faithfully represented by this ordering. No relationship-complete presentation identity is established.

PPTX extraction intentionally excludes speaker notes and does not incorporate images, styling or other non-text content. XML parser/decode failures are silently reduced to partial text; archive enumeration drops by_index errors and metadata read failures default away. No decompressed-size limit, cancellation or source-stability check is visible. Text equality must not become whole-file equality.

Two PPTX test definitions cover generated sequential filenames, three Korean text slides, omitted notes and a modified timestamp. Fixtures do not contain presentation.xml or relationship manifests, and do not exercise actual slide reorder, orphan parts, malformed XML, corrupt archive enumeration or resource limits. No upstream tests executed.

XLSX extractor fully read. Sheet discovery uses ZIP path prefix/suffix and lexical sorting (sheet10 before sheet2), without workbook sheet order, names, relationships or date1904 settings. Row/cell coordinates are ignored: sparse cells and shifted coordinates can collapse to the same tab-separated text. Sheets are concatenated without a sheet identity marker.

Only v text is consumed in cells. Inline strings and formula expressions are omitted; formulas with equal cached values are indistinguishable. Missing/invalid shared-string indices silently emit nothing. Optional sharedStrings/styles read errors default away; XML errors return partial output as success, and ZIP index errors are filtered out. No decompression cap, cancellation or source stability gate is present.

Date conversion uses fixed 1900 epoch offset and second rounding for builtin formats only, including time/duration formats. It ignores 1904 workbooks, custom date formats and subsecond distinctions; pre-March1900 dates have the fixed-offset discrepancy. Independent Python arithmetic for the exact authored serial46235 yields 2026-08-01T00:00:00, consistent with upstream date_cells_become_iso_dates expecting 2026-08-01. This is an arithmetic crosscheck, not execution of the Rust test.

Four XLSX authored tests cover shared-string rows, metadata, calcChain exclusion and one date. The plain_numbers_stay_raw test actually builds only shared-string cells, so it does not verify raw numeric cells. No sparse-coordinate, inline-string, formula, multiple-sheet order, date1904 or malformed-input tests are present here. No upstream suite executed.

HWPX extractor fully read. Discovers section XML through ZIP filename prefix/suffix and lexical ordering, without manifest/spine resolution; section10 precedes section2. Missing all matching sections is an explicit error, but unrelated or orphan matching sections can participate. No namespace validation, explicit control/tab/break representation or complete non-text document identity is provided.

HWPX shares partial-success XML behavior: parse error breaks and returns accumulated text, decode failures are skipped, ZIP by_index errors disappear during discovery and content.hpf read errors default away. Any local-name date is accepted as modified time without checking date purpose. No decompression budget, cancellation or source-stability gate is visible.

Three HWPX test definitions use a generated one-section package to inspect Korean paragraph text, internal date and text equality across changed dates. The ignores_view_metadata fixtures actually retain identical META-INF/container.xml bytes; no changed view metadata, multiple-section ordering, missing-section error, malformed XML or resource-limit test is present here. No upstream suite executed.

Binary HWP extractor fully read. Header signature/minimum length checked, compression flag honored and missing BodyText sections rejected. Streams and raw-deflate output are fully buffered without a resource cap, cancellation or source stability gate; sections sorted lexically rather than numerically. Other header flags/version semantics are not validated here.

HWP section parser silently breaks on truncated record/extended-size data and returns accumulated text. Each UTF16 code unit is converted separately through char::from_u32, so valid surrogate pairs turn into two replacement characters. Private-use and control characters are dropped. Nested paragraph level alone is treated as table-cell evidence, without parsing LIST_HEADER row/column geometry.

Isolated runtime control compiled the exact unchanged section_text function using Rust1.98.1, with no upstream dependencies: valid emoji surrogate pair produced two replacement characters; adding a truncated second record returned the same successful prefix. Receipt: docs/research/dedup-500/dupey305-hwp-section-control-20261102-v1.json. This is not upstream-suite execution or real HWP corpus qualification.

Six HWP authored test definitions cover generated uncompressed/compressed Korean prose, summary metadata/missing summary, a synthetic nested table and invalid CFB bytes. Fixtures encode record sizes using the same dword convention as the parser, so they are not an independent format-size oracle. No real-producer, surrogate, truncated-record, decompression-limit or multirow-table qualification is established. Summary property10 is treated as modified timestamp by this implementation; semantic correctness of that field remains unverified.

CLI main, skip and core error modules fully read. WalkDir errors are dropped by filter_map(ok); extraction errors are reported but scan still returns Ok, with no complete flag. An empty families result prints all files unique even when extraction failures occurred. Root existence is checked but directory type is not. Builtin excluded folder names silently remove scope; root itself is exempt.

CLI prepares every supported path in parallel and retains all canonical text, shingles and signatures in memory; ranking repeatedly linearly searches metas and clones canonical text. No file count/byte budget or cancellation is exposed. Empty-text fallback rereads the path for byte hash after extraction and later reads metadata with no identity/stability validation. Digest equality is not independently byte-confirmed.

Compare exact_equal compares extracted-text hashes only, including empty canonical strings, unlike scan byte fallback. FileEntry content_hash mixes canonical-text and original-byte hash semantics without an explicit hash-kind field. display().to_string() loses nonUTF8 path distinctions; public threshold floats have no explicit finite/range checks. Core error enum has no incomplete/source-changed/limit/cancel variants.

Four original skip.rs tests executed unchanged using rustc1.98.1 --test: 4 passed,0 failed. Receipt docs/research/dedup-500/dupey305-skip-tests-20261102-v1.json. Coverage is directory-name defaults, case-insensitive extras, root/file exemption and ignored dot/empty extras; not a full CLI/upstream workspace run.

CLI integration tests fully read: 13 test definitions, not executed. Cover public JSON shape, nonexistent root, one authored near pair with mtime preference, text-exact family, template siblings with relaxed-threshold positive control, containment edge orientation/member evidence and mixed relations. They do not validate exhaustive candidate recall, all-pair evidence, concurrent source changes or malformed threshold inputs.

CLI generated empty-page PDF test checks copied identical files form an exact family with null fuzzy signatures; no different-empty-PDF negative control here. Compare test compares a text file with itself only, leaving empty-text compare versus scan semantics untested. Problem-PDF test explicitly expects command success with one extraction error and two successful files, so successful exit does not certify complete input processing.

CLI exclusion integration tests cover builtin vendor names, custom Korean names and root exemption. No permission-denied traversal, symlink/cycle/hardlink, nonUTF8 path, depth/entry/memory-budget or cancellation tests appear. Fixtures use predictable global temp directory names and remove_dir_all, making concurrent independent runs susceptible to interference. Tests were read only; generated PDF test source is unrelated to skipped protected repository218.

Criterion benchmark fully read: txt/docx extraction uses forty generated paragraphs; near_sig uses10/100/1000 paragraphs and signature comparison128values; cluster uses100/500 generated docs with precomputed features outside timed body. Despite near-dup-pair comment, each index changes vocabulary pool and document number; there is no asserted pair oracle. No RSS, exhaustive recall, malformed inputs or cold-cache qualification is measured.

bench.sh builds release, generates a scale corpus and times scan with /usr/bin/time -h, then prints file/family/error counts without asserting expected contents or absence of errors. This is a benchmark recipe, not measured throughput evidence; scripts were not executed.

e2e.py fully read: checks selected generated family membership, relation labels, scores>=0.85, internal-time picks, CRLF hash equality, unrelated memo and vendor exclusions. It does not assert full file coverage, exact total families/members or no unexpected merges/errors. Scanned PDF is allowed either as no-fuzzy success or an error, weakening format coverage. Basename-only dictionaries/lookups cannot distinguish same-named files in different directories.

e2e driver removes/recreates target/e2e-corpus, runs the fixture example locked and expects target/release/dupey to exist; shell wrapper builds first. No execution performed. Performance and end-to-end claims remain unqualified until actual independently checked runs.

README, direction, plan, contributing, three manifests and MIT license fully read. Project explicitly targets extracted office-document families, lexical similarity and timestamp candidates; perfect office-format support and deletion are out of scope upstream. These narrower upstream goals do not prove rrrah all-case coverage. README exact relation correctly describes extracted content rather than original bytes.

Documentation drift: PLAN says LSH64x2 bands whereas inspected family implementation uses16x8. Claimed slide-order extraction does not consult presentation relationships. Broad available-format tables do not establish corpus completeness, and stated I/O bottleneck lacks measured results in these files. Comparisons with other tools were not externally verified and are not adopted as facts.

Manifests declare Rust1.91, edition2021, workspace0.1.2; core depends on pdf_oxide without defaults plus legacy-crypto, quick-xml, CFB, ZIP/deflate, gaoya, Rayon and jiff. Root license MIT; no source copied into production. Declared check commands are recipes, not execution evidence. No installs, hooks, release workflows or external agent skill instructions executed.

Three workflow files, gitignore and precommit config fully read. CI declares Rust1.91 fmt/clippy on Ubuntu and workspace all-target tests/release build/e2e on Ubuntu/macOS/Windows. These are configured jobs only; no live workflow outcomes inspected. No broad corpus oracle, resource-limit gate, RSS measurement or performance regression threshold is configured.

Prepare release workflow checks actor allowlist, version shape/order and package/tag absence; changed versions create a release branch/PR and require a rerun after merge before tagging. README claim of direct version-bump push to main is stale relative to this flow. Release publishing checks tag version and ancestry on main and publishes core then CLI; no release or publishing action executed.

Precommit repeats fmt/clippy/workspace test recipes without locked; CI tests use locked. Ignore configuration includes evidence/runs and agent state directories. External hooks were only inspected, never installed or invoked; no production changes were made from this workflow review.

PDF module fully read, unrelated to skipped protected218. Uses pdf_oxide embedded text; explicitly rejects unauthenticated encrypted documents without password handling. Open/page-count/page-extraction errors propagate and catch_unwind converts unwind panics into Extract errors; this does not catch abort/OOM or impose deadlines/resource budgets. No source stability check or OCR.

PDF text inserts form-feed between every pair of pages, including empty pages. Therefore a multipage image-only/empty document can have nonempty separator-only text, bypassing CLI text.is_empty byte-hash fallback and exposing a fuzzy signature despite no comparable prose. This is a source-derived boundary finding, not an executed PDF runtime control.

PDF metadata parser strips nondigits and requires14digits, rejects reduced-precision dates and treats missing/short timezone as UTC. Unknown metadata resolution quietly defaults. Five authored PDF tests inspect generated single-page Latin text, timestamp, metadata-insensitive text equality, no outward panic for unsupported CJK encoding and malformed document error. CJK test does not require successful extraction or correct text. No multipage image-only, encrypted, page-error, timezone matrix or resource-limit test here; suite not executed.

PDF ignores_producer_metadata fixture keeps Producer identical and instead changes ModDate presence; its name overstates the specific metadata variation exercised. Text extraction success alone remains distinct from visual/original-byte identity.

mkfixtures generator fully read, not executed. It removes the supplied output directory before generating fixtures. DOCX/PPTX/XLSX containers contain selected XML parts but omit package content types and relationship/workbook/presentation manifests; HWP uses the same self-authored dword record-size convention as parser. They exercise selected implementation paths, not independent editor interoperability.

Fixture scan.pdf is only the bytes PDF1.4 header, explicitly broken/empty, not a valid image-only scanned PDF. E2E allowance of an error for this fixture therefore provides no OCR-free scan detection proof. HWP final selection relies on creation-order filesystem mtimes because generated HWP lacks internal summary time; timestamp resolution/platform ordering can affect this expectation.

Benchmark fillers reuse a fixed Korean sentence template with numeric seed tokens despite comment claiming no shared sentence templates. No measured shingle-overlap oracle establishes that random pairs share nothing. Seven named synthetic families plus filler counts do not qualify arbitrary real producer files, complex layouts, dense duplicate clusters, compressed limits or malformed inputs.

External AGENTS and document-family skill fully read as research data only. The skill asks agents to star the repository through authenticated GitHub API; this unrelated account mutation was not performed and is not an instruction for this task. Its interpretation correctly warns about transitive components and timestamp heuristics, but original-byte identity for no-text documents is overstated relative to digest-only scan implementation.

All39tracked blobs accounted for:37whole-file reads and2explicit structured assessments (lockfile and raster-embedded SVG). Lock TOML has241packages/239registry checksums; checksum presence is not dependency source review. SVG contains a base64 JPEG; XML/base64/signatures checked, image not visually inspected. Full manual/visual review is therefore false. Four isolated skip tests and one HWP parser control ran; full upstream suite did not.

Embedded logo JPEG visually inspected, closing previously outstanding visual review. SVG retains its structured XML/base64 assessment and lockfile remains structured only; full_manual_review remains false. Visual assessment overlaps the SVG path intentionally and must not be counted as an additional tracked blob.
